sources.entry: sysctl kernel numa_balancing - Defines the hinting-fault sampling behind automatic balancing and tiering, and warns the overhead may not pay off.

summary.title: Documentation for /proc/sys/kernel/
summary.one_liner: A reference for the Linux kernel's /proc/sys/kernel sysctl knobs, including what numa_balancing, core_pattern, panic and hung-task settings do and their allowed values.
takeaways: numa_balancing is a bitmask: 0 disables it, 1 enables normal NUMA balancing, 2 enables memory tiering, and it works by unmapping pages and trapping page faults to sample accesses.
The page notes that the unmapping and fault overhead is not guaranteed to be offset by better locality, and that workloads already bound to NUMA nodes should disable it.
core_pattern supports format specifiers like %p, %e, %t and %h, and a leading '|' pipes core dumps to a user-space program.
Many kernel sysctls (dmesg_restrict, kptr_restrict, io_uring_disabled, hung_task_*) control security or detection behaviour and have documented default values.
summary.summary: This is the official kernel.org reference page for the sysctl files under /proc/sys/kernel. It describes each knob in alphabetical order, giving its purpose, accepted values and defaults, with tables for multi-value settings. The numa_balancing entry explains the page-fault-based sampling used for NUMA and memory tiering balancing and warns that the overhead is not universally repaid. The page is reference material rather than a tutorial, and the excerpt provided ends partway through the panic entry.
